module.purpose: Provides a factory creating an unsorted entity state adapter that mutates Immer draft state to add, set, update, remove, and upsert entities while preserving insertion order.
module.summary: This file exports a single factory function that builds an entity state adapter for managing an unsorted normalized collection. Inside the factory, numerous internal mutator functions operate directly on Immer draft state, handling single and bulk add, set, update, remove, and upsert operations. The adapter wraps these mutators with operator creators to present a consistent interface. It maintains parity between an ids array (insertion order) and an entities dictionary, and correctly rebuilds ids when an update changes an entity's id.
module.businessContext: Part of a Redux/Immer entity adapter toolkit for normalized state. Failure breaks unsorted entity collection management in consuming stores.
functions: createUnsortedStateAdapter (~L19-204): Factory returning unsorted entity state adapter with mutating operators
addOneMutably (~L24-33): Add single entity if its id is absent

setOneMutably (~L46-52): Assign single entity overwriting any existing

removeOneMutably (~L76-78): Remove one entity by delegating to removeMany
removeManyMutably (~L80-95): Delete many entities and filter ids

updateManyMutably (~L131-170): Merge and apply multiple updates
upsertOneMutably (~L172-174): Upsert one entity via upsertMany

mutationOfArg: All *Mutably functions mutate the passed draft state.ids and state.entities directly
addOneMutably pushes key to state.ids and assigns state.entities[key]
removeManyMutably deletes entity entries and reassigns filtered state.ids
setAllMutably resets state.ids=[] and state.entities={} before populating
updateManyMutably may rebuild state.ids from entity values when ids change

moduleContractTests.scenario: An adapter with addOne is called with a new entity not yet in state
moduleContractTests.then: state.ids contains the selected ID of entityA and state.entities maps that ID to entityA
moduleContractTests.rationale: Verifies the foundational insert path that all other add/upsert operations depend on.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An adapter with addOne is called with an entity whose selected ID already exists
moduleContractTests.then: state.entities[id] remains oldEntity and state.ids length is unchanged
moduleContractTests.rationale: Guards idempotency of addOne which is critical for incremental data loading.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An adapter with addMany is called with an array of new entities
moduleContractTests.then: state.ids contains both selected IDs and state.entities has both entities mapped
moduleContractTests.rationale: Validates batch insertion without partial application or ordering issues.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An adapter with setOne is called with an entity whose ID already exists but has different data
moduleContractTests.then: state.entities[1] is updated to updatedEntity and state.ids still contains 1 once
moduleContractTests.rationale: Ensures setOne performs replacement rather than append, distinguishing it from addOne.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An adapter with setAll is called with a new set of entities when existing entities are present
given: const initialState = { ids: [1, 2, 3], entities: { 1: e1, 2: e2, 3: e3 } }
moduleContractTests.then: state.ids is exactly [idB, idC] and state.entities has only entityB and entityC
moduleContractTests.rationale: Confirms setAll performs full replacement, not merge, which is the semantic distinction from setMany.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An adapter with removeOne is called with an ID that exists in state
given: const initialState = { ids: [1, 2], entities: { 1: e1, 2: e2 } }
moduleContractTests.then: state.ids is [2] and state.entities no longer has key 1
moduleContractTests.rationale: Validates the core removal path used by removeMany and indirectly by updateMany when ID changes.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An adapter with removeAll is called on a non-empty state
given: const initialState = { ids: [1, 2, 3], entities: { 1: e1, 2: e2, 3: e3 } }
moduleContractTests.rationale: Ensures complete state reset with no residual entity references.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An adapter with updateOne is called with an update whose changes do not alter the selected ID
given: const initialState with entity at id 1
moduleContractTests.then: state.entities[1].name is 'newName' and id 1 remains in state.ids
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins the update-without-key-change path which is the most common update scenario.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An adapter with upsertOne is called with an entity whose ID is not in state
moduleContractTests.then: state.ids contains the selected ID and state.entities maps that ID to newEntity
moduleContractTests.rationale: Validates the insert branch of upsert, distinguishing it from addOne behavior.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An adapter with upsertOne is called with an entity whose ID already exists
given: const initialState with entity at id 1
moduleContractTests.then: state.entities[1] is replaced by modifiedEntity and id 1 remains at its position
moduleContractTests.rationale: Validates the update branch of upsert, ensuring it merges or replaces correctly.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An adapter with upsertMany is called with a mix of new and existing entities
given: const initialState with entity at id 1
moduleContractTests.then: existing entity is updated and both new entities are added with no duplicates
moduleContractTests.rationale: Ensures upsertMany correctly partitions inputs into add vs update paths without conflicts.

given: const initialState = { ids: [1, 2, 3], entities: { 1: e1, 2: e2, 3: e3 } }

moduleContractTests.rationale: Validates bulk removal with graceful handling of non-existent IDs.

units.name: createUnsortedStateAdapter

detail.name: createUnsortedStateAdapter
detail.signature: export function createUnsortedStateAdapter<T, Id extends EntityId>(selectId: IdSelector<T, Id>): EntityStateAdapter<T, Id>
preconditions: selectId must be a callable IdSelector<T, Id> function that maps any entity of type T to a primitive Id suitable for use as an entities map key
postconditions: Returns an EntityStateAdapter<T, Id> containing exactly 12 state operator methods (addOne, addMany, setOne, setMany, setAll, updateOne, updateMany, upsertOne, upsertMany, removeOne, removeMany, removeAll), each delegating to a corresponding *Mutably internal function wrapped via createStateOperator or createSingleArgumentStateOperator
Each returned operator, when invoked with (state, ...) arguments, produces a new state object by applying the wrapped mutability function to an immer draft derived from the input state
invariants: Every operator on the returned adapter maintains the invariant that state.ids and state.entities remain in sync (each id in ids has a matching key in entities, and each key in entities appears in ids)
Entity IDs remain unique within state.ids (no duplicate entries)
The returned adapter object is a fresh instance created per call to the factory, with no shared mutable state between invocations
edgeCases: If selectId is null, undefined, or not a function, the factory still returns an adapter object but any operator invocation will throw a TypeError at runtime when calling selectIdValue
If selectId returns the same key for different entities, later entities overwrite earlier ones in the same state.entities slot
If state.entities or state.ids is accessed before any operator is called, the structure reflects whatever was passed in (factory does not initialize state)
setAllMutably resets state.ids to an empty array and state.entities to an empty object before adding new entities, discarding all prior state

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: The factory performs no input validation on selectId; if it is null, undefined, or not a function, the factory still returns an adapter object, but any operator invocation will throw a TypeError at runtime when attempting to call selectIdValue

detail.summary: Factory that constructs an EntityStateAdapter whose internal mutability helpers are wrapped as immutable state operators via createStateOperator and createSingleArgumentStateOperator, enabling unsorted entity state management where insertion order is not preserved.

specTests.when: createUnsortedStateAdapter is called with that selector
specTests.then: it returns an object with exactly 12 callable operator methods: addOne, addMany, setOne, setMany, setAll, updateOne, updateMany, upsertOne, upsertMany, removeOne, removeMany, removeAll

specTests.when: createUnsortedStateAdapter is called with that invalid selectId and the returned adapter's addOne operator is invoked with a valid entity and state
specTests.then: the addOne operator throws a TypeError at runtime when it attempts to call selectIdValue with the invalid selector

detail.name: addOneMutably
detail.signature: function addOneMutably(entity: T, state: R): void
preconditions: entity must have an identifier selectable via selectId (used by selectIdValue)
state must have an `ids` array and an `entities` object/record property
postconditions: If the computed key is not already a property of state.entities, state.ids has key appended and state.entities[key] equals entity
If the key already exists in state.entities, state is left unchanged and function returns without effect
invariants: state.ids length equals number of keys in state.entities after mutation
No duplicate keys are introduced into state.ids
edgeCases: Entity whose key already exists in state.entities: function returns early, no mutation occurs
Entity with new key: key is pushed to state.ids and entity stored in state.entities
stateMutations: state.ids (push key)
state.entities (assign property key to entity)
detail.summary: Adds a single entity to the provided state mutably by appending its id to state.ids and setting state.entities[key] to the entity, skipping the operation if the key already exists in state.entities.

specTests.then: state remains unchanged (ids length 1, entities.a === existing)

preconditions: state is a valid unsorted state object with ids and entities maps
key is a valid identifier of type Id
postconditions: state is mutated such that the entity with given key is removed (via removeManyMutably)

units.name: removeManyMutably

detail.name: removeManyMutably
detail.signature: function removeManyMutably(keys: readonly Id[], state: R): void
preconditions: state must be a valid object with both `entities` and `ids` properties
each key in `keys` must be a valid Id type
postconditions: all entities corresponding to the provided keys are removed from `state.entities`
if any removal occurred, `state.ids` is filtered to contain only IDs still present in `state.entities`
invariants: state.ids and state.entities remain consistent (ids only references keys in entities)
no mutation occurs if none of the keys are present in state.entities
edgeCases: if `keys` is empty, no mutation occurs
if none of the `keys` exist in `state.entities`, no mutation occurs
if duplicate keys are provided, each is processed independently without error
stateMutations: state.entities: deletes entries for each key found
state.ids: filters entries when at least one entity was removed
detail.summary: Removes multiple entities by their IDs from the state, mutating the entities map and filtering the IDs array to retain only existing entity IDs.

units.name: removeAllMutably

detail.name: removeAllMutably
preconditions: state is a non-null object (the entity state to clear)
postconditions: state.ids is replaced with a new empty array []
state.entities is replaced with a new empty object {}
state is mutated in place; the caller's reference reflects the cleared values
invariants: The state object reference is preserved (Object.assign mutates the target in place rather than replacing it)
edgeCases: If state is null or undefined, Object.assign throws a TypeError because it cannot use null/undefined as a target
Calling on an already-empty state is an idempotent reset (ids stays [], entities stays {})

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Throws a TypeError if state is null or undefined; otherwise clears state in place

stateMutations: Overwrites state.ids with a new empty array []
Overwrites state.entities with a new empty object {}
Mutates the passed state object in place (no new state object is allocated)
detail.summary: Given a Redux entity state object, this function resets it to an empty state by clearing the ids list and the entities map, mutating the provided state object in place so callers observe the cleared values through their existing reference.

specTests.then: state.ids becomes an empty array (length 0), state.entities becomes an empty object with no own keys, and the original state object reference is preserved (mutated in place)

detail.name: takeNewKey
detail.signature: function takeNewKey(keys: { [id: string]: Id }, update: Update<T, Id>, state: R): boolean
preconditions: state.entities is a record keyed by Id
update has shape { id: Id, changes: Partial<T> }
selectId closure available to extract Id from T
postconditions: If original entity exists, state.entities contains merged entity under newKey (old key removed if changed)
Returns true if key changed for existing entity, false otherwise (including missing entity)
invariants: state.entities remains a record mapping Id to T
keys maps old id to new id only when key changed
edgeCases: update.id absent in state.entities: returns false, no mutations
update.changes empty: newKey equals update.id, returns false, entity reassigned
update.changes alters selected id: entity re-keyed and keys updated
stateMutations: state.entities (assigns updated at newKey, deletes old key if changed)
keys (sets old->new mapping if changed)
detail.summary: Ensures that an existing entity in state is updated with provided changes and, if the updated entity's selected id differs from the original, the old id mapping is recorded in keys and the entity is re-keyed; returns true iff the key changed.

specTests.then: returns true, state.entities['2'] = {id:'2',name:'b'}, state.entities['1'] deleted, keys['1'] === '2'

state.ids (replaced with mapped ids if any key changed)
